summary.headline: Fratelli H1 FY27 net revenue rose about 10% to INR91.4 crores and EBITDA turned to a INR1.4 crore profit from a loss of about INR1 crore.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 net revenue from operations was INR91.4 crores versus INR83.4 crores, up about 10%, with H1 gross margin at 78% and EBITDA swinging to a profit of INR1.4 crores. Q2 was softer: UP was down about 30% on an H1 basis after the excise policy change, Karnataka was subdued, and bottle growth excluding those two states was about 6%. RTD (Shotgun) revenue doubled to about INR18 crores in H1 and the company is targeting 200,000 cases by end FY27. Management also announced a rights issue of up to INR29.87 crores, with promoters subscribing to their full entitlement, and gave no revenue guidance until the Q3 call.

segments.name: Luxury wine (J'NOON, SETTE)
segments.commentary: J'NOON grew 23% in H1, but overall luxury grew only about 4-5% because SETTE was flat in H1 and degrew slightly in CSD. Management expects SETTE repeat orders in Q3.

segments.name: Premium wine (Shiraz, UP)
segments.commentary: UP is a top-seven market and is down about 30% for the company on an H1 basis after the excise policy change, with the new policy effective 1 April. Management expects Q3 to be slightly better and Q3/Q4 to be similar to last year's H2.

segments.name: RTD (Shotgun, TiLT)
segments.commentary: Shotgun is nearly 100,000 cases in H1, with a target of 200,000 cases by FY27 end; it is in about 11,000 of 32,000 touchpoints. TiLT is among leading RTD brands in CSD within six months of launch.

segments.name: Value and southern markets
segments.commentary: Value portfolio delivered steady performance, led by southern markets. Growth was strong in Kerala, Goa, Orissa, Telangana (one of the strongest markets in H1), and Pondicherry.

segments.name: HoReCa vs retail (bottles)
segments.commentary: Bottles split is about 65:35 HoReCa to retail; RTD is about 97-98% retail. Company claims over 35% share in key on-trade markets and above 50% in some.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin guidance for FY27 kept at 77-80%.
Shotgun target of 200,000 cases by end FY27, more than double FY26.
Overall revenue guidance deferred until the Q3 call; no FY27/FY28 growth number given.
Net profitability expected from Q1 or Q2 FY28, subject to trajectory and other factors remaining constant.
RTD and new brands expected to start contributing to cash flow and results from mid-FY28.
Brand spend to stay at 8-10% of sales (RTD about 9-10%) for two to three more quarters; overall bottles spend about 5-6% of net sales.
Vision 2030 EBITDA margin guidance of 20% not revised; company said it is close to EBITDA breakeven at current run rate.
Tamil Nadu TASMAC listing expected to get a positive update by end of Q3; Jammu & Kashmir also targeted this year.
Management expects revenue potential of INR350-400 crores against about half that today.
capex_capacity: RTD capacity is sufficient to double current volumes, so no near-term RTD capex is needed.

Rights issue proceeds (up to INR29.87 crores) include funding winery equipment and oak barrels at subsidiary/operating companies, alongside balance-sheet strengthening, settling trade payables (about INR8.6 crores) and general corporate purposes.
Vineyard tourism project (10 acres owned, about 200 acres of leased vineyards under long-term dry lease from promoter family) has been deferred; viability to be re-examined in FY28.
Footprint: available in 28 states, 32,000 touchpoints; four new international markets added in H1, taking the total to 18 countries.
demand_pricing: Delhi was subdued in Q1 but recovered in Q2, which moved it to positive growth; H1 Delhi growth was about 1%.
Karnataka, a top-six market, was subdued due to industry headwinds; UP and Karnataka together drove the bottle dip.
Excluding UP and Karnataka, bottle growth at H1 was about 6-7%.
HoReCa: Bombay subdued for six months; Delhi, Bangalore, West Bengal and Hyderabad remain strong.
Management is evaluating price hikes across markets after Q3, testing elasticity against each market's competitive landscape.
Imported wines: India-EU FTA keeps duty at 150% on wines up to EUR 2.5; management sees no major shake-up.

qa_highlights.question: What share of luxury does J'NOON hold, and why is luxury growth only 4% when J'NOON grew 23%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SETTE was flat in H1 after a record H1 last year that included its CSD launch, with a slight CSD degrowth, so total luxury grew about 4-5%. A SETTE repeat pipeline is expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How large is UP, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: UP is a top-seven market and was among the fastest-growing for four years. H1 was slow due to the excise policy change, Q3 looks slightly better, and the new policy applies from 1 April, so the year will be a challenge while Q3 and Q4 should be similar to last year's H2.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin fell to about 76.7% in Q2, and other expenses rose about 44%. Why?
qa_highlights.answer: The mix shift to RTD, which was about INR18.5 crores in the quarter, plus a moderate industry-wide sugar cost increase lowered margin. Other expenses rose on RTD marketing at about 9% of RTD sales. FY27 margin guidance of 77-80% is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth excluding UP and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: At H1, bottle growth excluding UP and Karnataka was about 6% (6-7% quoted). Management did not give a quarter-on-quarter figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay down debt with the rights issue, and when will cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no major debt reduction planned; the rights issue creates some working-capital relief. Cash flow should improve from VAT refunds (about INR18 crores stuck in Maharashtra and Karnataka), Telangana receivables, bulk wine inventory reduction, and RTD scale-up from mid-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: When will net profit turn positive on a quarterly basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net profitability from Q1 or Q2 FY28, provided trends hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Shotgun/RTD plan for Tamil Nadu and the Vision 2030 EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: The TASMAC file is under process, with an update expected by end of Q3; MRP will be shared in December. Vision 2030 20% EBITDA margin guidance was kept, with incremental revenue expected to lift margins as overheads stay flat.

risks_watch: UP excise policy effects persist until the new policy starts on 1 April; UP is down about 30% at H1.

Working capital is strained: about INR18 crores of VAT receivables are stuck, DSO is high, bulk wine inventory is above target, and the company is paying roughly twice its cash interest outflow relative to operating cash flow (analyst figure, about INR5 crores operating cash flow last year).
Cash flow was weak against interest costs; management has not committed to a debt reduction path.
Gross margin pressure as RTD mix rises, with RTD marketing spend at 8-10% of sales for two to three quarters.
Luxury growth lags J'NOON, with SETTE flat in H1 and CSD softness.
Pending Q3 update on TASMAC listing, new product launches, and FY27/FY28 revenue guidance.
Rights issue closes 17 November; promoters will backstop any unsubscribed portion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story (RTD scale, Shotgun, new markets, luxury and premium brands) but cautious on near-term numbers: revenue guidance was withheld until Q3, and several answers on margins, debt and cash flow were deflected or framed as future-year outcomes.
key_quotes: Revenue is growing and profitability is improving.
We are on course to hit 200,000 cases by the end of FY27, which will be more than double our previous year performance.
We don't see a major reduction in debt at the moment.
So, our gross margin guidance, which has been between 77% to 80%, remains intact.

growth.why: No revenue guidance until the Q3 call; H1 FY27 net revenue rose about 10% to INR91.4 crore, with UP down about 30% and the Shotgun RTD target of 200,000 cases by FY27-end unbacked by specific capacity, and the vineyard tourism project deferred with no capacity added.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin held at 77-80% for FY27 but Q2 fell to about 76.7% from 79-80%, and RTD marketing at 8-10% of sales continues for two to three more quarters; margin expansion depends on incremental revenue lifting operating leverage toward Vision 2030 20% EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: RTD capacity is sufficient to double current volumes, no near-term RTD capex is needed, and the vineyard tourism project is deferred to FY28 review.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 net revenue up about 10% to INR91.4 crore and bottle growth ex-UP and Karnataka about 6-7%, but UP is down about 30% until the new excise policy starts 1 April; Shotgun targets 200,000 cases by FY27 end from nearly 100,000 in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is deferred; RTD capacity covers double current volumes, and rights issue proceeds (up to INR29.87 crore) fund winery equipment and oak barrels plus working-capital and payables (about INR8.6 crore) rather than new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance until the Q3 call, FY27 gross margin guide held at 77-80%, and Q2 gross margin about 76.7% sits below that range's midpoint.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance is withheld until Q3, UP is down about 30% in H1 with the new excise policy only from 1 April, and about INR18 crore of VAT receivables are stuck, so a weaker FY27 revenue framing is plausible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects RTD and new brands to contribute to cash flow and results from mid-FY28; four new international markets added in H1 taking the total to 18 countries, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Net profitability from Q1 or Q2 FY28
rows.why: Management expects net profit from Q1 or Q2 FY28 subject to trajectory, while H1 EBITDA is only a INR1.4 crore profit and cash interest is roughly twice operating cash flow (analyst figure, about INR5 crore operating cash flow last year).

rows.label: VAT receivable recovery and working-capital relief
rows.why: About INR18 crore of VAT is stuck in Maharashtra and Karnataka with only a small tranche received, and the rights issue gives some working-capital relief, but no debt reduction is planned.

rows.label: TASMAC listing in Tamil Nadu
rows.why: Management expects a positive update on the TASMAC listing by end Q3 with MRP shared in December, but the listing is not yet confirmed and Telangana and southern states are already growing.
